newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-GUARDIOLA LEADS SPAIN TO 2-0 WIN OVER YUGOSLAVIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GUARDIOLA LEADS SPAIN TO 2-0 WIN OVER YUGOSLAVIA.

text.p: Barcelona midfielder Josep Guardiola led Spain to an impressive 2-0 victory over Yugoslavia in an exciting European group six World Cup qualifier on Saturday.
Guardiola, who struggles to hold down a place for both club and country, first scored from a penalty and then set up Real Madrid's Raul Gonzalez for the second.

The result means Spain close the gap on Yugoslavia at the top of the group to two points. It was the first defeat in the qualifying stage for the visitors, who have 12 points from five games. Spain have 10 from four.

Guardiola had only come into the game as a replacement for Real Madrid's Fernando Hierro. But his composure contrasted with that of Yugoslav Predrag Mijatovic, who was clearly unnerved by jeering from the fans at the ground where he made his name as a Valencia player before moving to Real Madrid in the close season.
